newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Solidarity launches electoral campaign.
newsitem.headline: Polish Solidarity launches electoral campaign.

text.p: Poland's opposition rightist Solidarity alliance launched its campaign for the September 21 polls on Sunday with promises to finish the country's market reforms and restore honesty to public life.

The Solidarity Election Action (AWS), which groups more than 30 small right-wing parties around the Solidarity trade union, pledged to combine pro-growth policies with social justice and Christian values, during its first electoral convention.

The group, whose members helped defeat communism in 1989 but lost power to ex-communists four years later due to internal quarrels, trotted out slogans like "Always: Poland, Freedom, Family" and "The Right Poland."

"The right Poland means fidelity to true values...right to private ownership, economic freedom and effective law," AWS leader Marian Krzaklewski said, opening the convention in the central city of Radom.

He confirmed his group's support for quick entry into NATO and the European Union but said the new, unified Europe must observe the national identity of each country. "We are for the Europe of fatherlands," he said.
Krzaklewski reiterated vows to speed up privatisation, lower taxes, reform the social security system and use housing construction as an engine of economic growth.
"In the next two years, about only 30 percent of the national assets should be in the state's hands and in four years -- 20 percent," he said. The state now controls about helf of the state assets.

The Solidarity's programme provides for speedily returning to former owners assets confiscated during cummunist rule and distributing privatisation coupons to all Poles, which would enable them to participate in the country's economic success.
Poland's economic growth, which started in 1992, is forecast to reach 5.5 percent this year.

In the process which the Solidarity calls "enfranchisement," the coupons could be exchanged for shares of firms undergoing privatisation and allocated to independent pension funds, to be created under a social security reform plan.

The AWS, advocating Catholic, pro-family values and opposing abortion, says Poland should undergo a moral renewal to get rid of people involved in the old system before 1989 who now portray themselves as pro-Western pragmatists.
The AWS, which has similar support as the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), says it would strive to reduce the role of former communists in the economy.
The alleged dominance of ex-communists in banks and large corporations is harmful for the economy, it says.
